summary: Scoped impersonation gateway for analytics ETL to copy GCS -> S3 with least-privilege and audit
description:
Issue summary:
We need a secure, auditable mechanism that allows long-running analytics ETL workers running in our AWS analytics-prod account to read objects from a GCS bucket in the GCP analytics-prod project and write them to an S3 bucket in the AWS account. The preferred flow is a short-lived impersonation gateway that performs token exchange/impersonation rather than provisioning long-lived keys in the ETL workers.

Impact:
- Current workaround uses service-account JSON in a secrets store which increases blast radius and requires manual rotations.
- ETL pipelines for nightly reports and feature-store materialization are blocked from migrating to the new partitioned job runner until a secure cross-cloud identity pattern is in place.
- Compliance wants CloudTrail / Cloud Audit logs tied to a single auditable gateway identity.

Environment:
- GCP project: analytics-prod (gcs: gs://redwood-analytics-prod-data)
- AWS account: analytics-prod (s3: s3://redwood-analytics-prod-landing)
- ETL runner: Kubernetes job in aws-prod EKS cluster (namespace: analytics-jobs)

Acceptance criteria / success conditions:
1) ETL pods do NOT have long-lived GCP service account keys.
2) ETL pods request ephemeral credentials from an internal gateway endpoint (mTLS + RBAC) and receive a short-lived token that allows reading a specific GCS prefix.
3) Gateway enforces per-job least-privilege scoping (object prefix and read-only) via IAM conditions and expires tokens within 15m.
4) All cross-cloud access is recorded in Cloud Audit Logs and CloudTrail associated with the gateway principal.
5) Terraform manifests (or a small module) are provided to create the gateway, IAM bindings, KMS encryption keys policies, and a small integration test that copies a test object.

Proposed implementation notes / suggestions:
- Use GCP service account impersonation (IAM serviceAccountTokenCreator) bound to a gateway compute identity in the GCP project. The gateway will request short-lived access tokens from GCP STS and sign requests for the ETL worker.
- On AWS side, the gateway runs in EKS and uses an IRSA role with minimal permissions to read from the internal secrets if necessary. ETL workers authenticate to gateway using mTLS (client certs issued by internal CA) or sigv4 to an ALB with mutual TLS.
- Evaluate AWS STS:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity for the reverse flow if we need to write to S3 under cross-account role; otherwise the ETL job can use its AWS role to write to S3 after retrieving object.
- Apply IAM Conditions on the GCP side to constrain access to resource.name.startsWith("projects/_/buckets/redwood-analytics-prod-data/objects/hourly/").
- KMS: Keys used for secrets or wrapped credentials must have key access restricted to gateway principal. Record key arn / key id in Terraform module outputs.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Must not allow the gateway to perform broader operations than token exchange (no owner/editor scopes).
- Audit logs and request ids must be forwarded to the central logging cluster and linked to the job id for traceability.
- Gateway issuer identity should be a service account with a narrow permission set and a descriptive name (e.g., redwood-analytics-impersonation-gw@analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com).

Work items / To-do (proposal):
- [ ] Create a minimal Terraform module in infra/iam-modules that:
      - creates gateway GCP service account and grants iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on target SA
      - creates IAM condition binding limiting object prefix and read action
      - provisions AWS IRSA role and optional cross-account role for S3 writes
- [ ] Build a small Go or Python gateway prototype that performs token exchange and exposes a single POST /v1/token endpoint.
- [ ] Integration test: job that requests token, downloads test file from GCS, writes to S3, validates checksums, and emits logs.
- [ ] Add audit log dashboard snippet and alert for failed impersonation attempts > 5/hr.

Related constraints / questions for infra/security:
- Can we rely on internal CA + mTLS for pod auth, or does security require OIDC-based pod identity (SPIRE / SPIFFE) integration?
- Are we allowed to create iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator bindings on analytics-prod service accounts from the EKS worker role? Need approval from cloud security.

References / links:
- Existing runbooks: https://confluence.internal.redwood/infra/runbooks/cross-cloud-iam (placeholder)
- Similar pattern: INT-30421 (scoped-readonly-cloud-trace-access) - use as a reference for approval flow
- Draft idea sketch: https://github.com/redwood/infra-templates/pull/999 (placeholder)

Please coordinate with: security@redwood, cloud-platform, and the analytics infra team.
comments: 2026-03-08 - Priya Shah: Filing this after a sync with Analytics product. Blocking migration of nightly ETL. Assigned to Riley for initial design.
2026-03-09 - Riley Chen: I'll prototype a gateway using python oauthlib. Need confirmation on whether mTLS is acceptable; security asked about SPIRE. Looping in @Samir Patel from Security.

2026-03-10 - Samir Patel: Security preference is OIDC-based pod identity (IRSA + Workload Identity Federation) over in-band mTLS certs. We can approve a narrow iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator binding if gated by IAM Conditions and audit forwarding.

2026-03-12 - Riley Chen: Prototype repo created: github.com/redwood/analytics-impersonation-gw. Added initial Terraform scaffolding. Next: run integration test in staging and provide KMS key ARNs for review.
